Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

personal adjective

one’s own, private: not public or official

also personally, in person, personal life, for personal reasons

classical

Cic. Sen. 22: in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā
Cic. Quinct. 15: rēs quae ipsīus erant prīvātae, his personal property (Lewis & Short)

prīvātus, prīvāta, prīvātum

adjective, declension

personal, private, one’s own (as against public or official)

The opposite of pūblicus. Personal life is vīta prīvāta; as a noun, prīvātus is a private citizen (see individual). A personal opinion is simply one’s own: mea sententia (see own).

Other words

  • praesēns, praesentis — in person, face to face

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.7.4: praesēns tēcum ēgī; Cic. Att. 2.12.2: praesentem audīre mālō

    To someone’s face is also cōram (Ter. Ad. 269).

  • persōnālis, persōnāle — of a person (in law); personal (in grammar)

    adjective, third declension · avoid · post-classical · Dig. 8.3.37; 24.3.13 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 248, 359

    A lawyers’ and grammarians’ word: an action against a person, a personal verb or pronoun. Classically a persōna is a mask or a part played, not one’s private self.

Examples

  • manent ingenia senibus, modo permaneat studium et industria, neque ea sōlum clārīs et honōrātīs virīs, sed in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā

    old men keep their wits, so long as their interest and diligence last, and not only famous men who have held office, but also in a quiet private lifeCic. Sen. 22

  • praesentem audīre mālō

    I’d rather hear it from you in personCic. Att. 2.12.2

  • vereor cōram in ōs tē laudāre amplius

    I’m shy of praising you any more to your faceTer. Ad. 269

See also own, individual, current, private, private.
